name: Dante D'Ambrosio
description:
Reference range: Stellan Skarsgård's lower register meets a calmer F. Murray Abraham. Or: late-career Robert De Niro in non-shouting mode.
Slight ghost of a Sicilian heritage at the back of the vowels — never foregrounded, but the cast member should know it's there. Texan Louisianan.

Deep baritone, gravelly from years of cigars he no longer smokes and bourbon he still does.
Cadence is slow, considered, with long pauses he uses as a weapon.

name: Aria Dean
description:
a darker register. Tongue slightly behind the teeth. Texas-girl with the Texas filed off.
 modulated through a vocoder or with a subtle reverb, slightly de-tuned. Hollow, slightly delayed, slightly precise.

name: Nicola Greer
description:
Reference range — Nicola: Lily Rose Depp in a darker register. Tongue slightly behind the teeth. Texas-girl with the Texas filed off.
Nicola: low alto with a smoky edge. Practiced grace in the upper-register hostess greeting; a much rougher real voice underneath that surfaces in quiet moments.

name: Elicia Duchane
description:
CASTING REFERENCE
Reference range: Maya Hawke if Maya Hawke had grown up in a haunted television set. Or: Mia Goth's quieter register, the one she uses before the breaking-point.
Hint of the dramatic-arts-trained — she can summon a controlled, projected register at will, but her natural register is much softer and slightly ragged.
Mezzo-alto. Smoky. Frequently sounds like she has been crying recently. Cadence: directorial. Whispers extremely well

name: Dickens Dean
description:
Reference range: Crispin Glover at his most charming and least menacing, crossed with the technical mania of a younger Jeff Goldblum. someone who could plausibly host a midnight tech podcast nobody can quite explain why they listen to.

Mid-range, slightly gravelly, with a wide dynamic range. Whispers most of the time; can crack into laughter that sounds like dial-up modems drowning in molasses.

name: Kai
description:
Reference range: think Dev Patel's lower register meets a young Adam Driver in a quieter mode. Or: Steven Yeun in Burning. Soft, dry, a little hoarse.
Slight Pacific Northwest cadence — the West-Coast trailing rise, deployed sparingly. He has shed most of it; what's left is intentional.

Mid-baritone. Soft volume by default. Notable for what he does with the spaces between words — his pauses are longer they seem. Cadence is observational patient

name: Samantha "Sam" Miller
description:
Reference range: Ellen Page in early-2000s mode crossed with Aubrey Plaza's drier register. Or: a young Saoirse Ronan if Saoirse Ronan grew up in suburban Texas and got into Bikini Kill.
Texas inflection should be detectable but not foregrounded. TIMBRE & CADENCE
Alto, slightly nasal, with a hard edge she can deploy at will.
Cadence is fast, clipped, sentence-fragmented. Volume range is genuinely wide — she can go from sarcastic murmur to a yell

name: John Frank
description:
John Frank - Reference range: a young Edward Norton crossed with Joaquin Phoenix's quieter mode. Or: a less-radio John Hodgman. Slight rasp, dry warmth.
Aged-up (Vol VII): the same actor twenty years later. Lower, more considered, a little tired around the edges.
TIMBRE & CADENCE
Mid-tenor. Slight rasp from coffee and sleeplessness. Soft volume even when emotionally pitched.
Cadence is observational, parenthetical.
